included.label: What's included
included.title: The routine jobs that keep a garden in shape
included.description: I focus on the practical essentials that keep a garden looking its best. That means tidy beds, neat edges, sensible pruning, and a clean finish every time I visit. I tailor each session to what actually needs doing rather than following a rigid checklist, because gardens change week to week with the weather. I also offer straightforward advice on seasonal tasks so you know what is coming up and can plan ahead. Cornwall's longer growing season means there is always something to stay on top of, and regular visits prevent small jobs from turning into big ones.

items.title: General tidy & reset
items.description: A quick refresh each visit that makes the whole garden feel looked after. I will clear fallen leaves, pick up debris, tidy around bins and sheds, and make sure nothing looks neglected. First impressions matter, and a general tidy is often what makes the biggest difference to how a garden feels day to day.

items.title: Weeding & bed care
items.description: Keeping beds weeded and clear gives your plants the space and light they need to thrive. I remove weeds by hand and hoe where appropriate, and I will flag anything that is spreading aggressively before it becomes a bigger problem. Cornwall's damp, mild climate means weeds can establish quickly, so regular attention here saves a lot of effort later.

items.title: Borders & edging
items.description: Crisp lawn edges and clean border lines instantly lift the look of any garden. I use a half-moon edger and line trimmer to keep boundaries sharp between lawn, beds, paths, and paving. This is one of those small details that makes a surprisingly big difference to the overall appearance.

items.title: Light pruning (as needed)
items.description: Light pruning on shrubs, climbers, and smaller plants to keep growth tidy and under control. I will cut back anything that is encroaching on paths or blocking light, and I will time pruning to suit the plant species so you are not accidentally removing next season's flowers. For larger pruning jobs or tree work, I will let you know and quote separately.

items.title: Green waste removal (optional)
items.description: Garden waste, clippings and prunings can be collected and removed by agreement. Green waste removal is £10 per dumpy bag. Quilliams is an Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202, and I confirm the agreed waste route and likely cost upfront.

items.title: Season-aware advice
items.description: Practical, season-aware advice on what needs doing next. Whether it is the right time to cut back perennials, when to mulch, or how to prepare beds for winter, I will keep you informed so nothing gets missed. Cornwall's climate is forgiving, but getting the timing right on seasonal tasks still makes a noticeable difference to how the garden performs.

plans.label: Regular care
plans.title: Choose a maintenance schedule that suits you
plans.description: Most of my garden maintenance customers in Cornwall choose fortnightly visits during the growing season, which runs from roughly March through to November here. Weekly visits suit larger gardens or those that need a consistently tidy appearance, while monthly visits work well for lower-maintenance gardens where you just want someone to keep on top of things. Visits are priced between £60 and £120 depending on garden size. I will recommend the right schedule based on your garden and what you want prioritised.

cards.title: Weekly visit
cards.description: Best for larger gardens or those where presentation needs to stay sharp at all times. Weekly visits keep everything under control so the garden always looks its best. Particularly useful during the fast-growing months from April to September when beds, borders, and lawns all need regular attention.

cards.title: Fortnightly visit
cards.description: The most popular option across my customers in Cornwall. Fortnightly visits give me enough time to cover everything that needs doing without the cost of weekly attendance. Your garden stays tidy and manageable, and I can adjust the schedule seasonally as growth slows down over winter.

cards.title: Monthly tidy
cards.description: A bigger, more thorough visit once a month to stop things drifting. This suits gardens that are relatively low-maintenance or where you do some of the lighter work yourself and just need someone to handle the bigger tasks regularly. I will prioritise the jobs that make the most visible difference each time.

cards.title: Seasonal refresh
cards.description: A focused tidy at the start of spring or autumn to set the garden up for what is ahead. Spring refreshes often involve cutting back winter growth, weeding beds, edging, and a general clear-up. Autumn visits focus on leaf clearance, cutting back perennials, and preparing borders for the cooler months.

items.question: What's included in garden maintenance?
items.answer: Garden maintenance covers the regular tasks that keep your garden looking its best. That typically includes lawn mowing, border weeding, hedge trimming, leaf clearance, light pruning, and general tidying. I tailor each visit to what actually needs doing at the time rather than running through a rigid checklist. Cornwall's longer growing season means gardens here stay active well into autumn and start early in spring, so consistent upkeep makes a real difference. Regular visits are priced between £60 and £120 per visit depending on garden size. I will always discuss what you want prioritised so your garden gets the attention where it matters most.

items.question: Do you offer regular visits?
items.answer: Yes, regular visits are one of the most popular things I offer. Most customers book fortnightly visits during the growing season, though some prefer weekly or monthly depending on the size of their garden and how quickly things grow. Regular visits are priced at £60 to £120 per visit depending on garden size. Booking regular slots means your garden never gets ahead of you, and it is more cost-effective than letting things build up and needing a big catch-up job. I keep a consistent schedule so you know when to expect me.

items.question: Can you remove green waste?
items.answer: Yes, green waste can be removed by agreement. Removal is charged at £10 per dumpy bag. Quilliams is an Environment Agency registered waste carrier (lower tier), CBDL582202. For regular maintenance customers, the waste produced each visit is usually manageable, and I confirm the agreed waste route and likely cost upfront.

items.question: Can you do a one-off tidy?
items.answer: Yes, one-off garden tidies are something I do regularly. Whether you have let things slip over winter, you are preparing a property for sale, or you just want a fresh start, I can come in and get everything back under control. This usually involves mowing, strimming, weeding, pruning, and clearing debris. The cost depends on the size of the garden and how much work is involved, so I will give you a clear quote after seeing the space. Many customers start with a one-off tidy and then move onto regular maintenance to keep things manageable.

items.question: Do you cover my area?
items.answer: I am based near Newquay and cover a good chunk of Cornwall, including Truro, St Austell, Bodmin, Padstow, Perranporth, and St Ives. If you are within that area, I can usually fit you in without any issue. If you are slightly further afield, feel free to get in touch anyway and I will let you know if I can help.
